content: During treatment with this medication, there is a very low but potential risk of developing cancer, such as lymphoma or skin cancer. This risk is higher in children, teenagers, and young adults. The risk may be related to the medication itself or the underlying medical condition being treated. It is essential to discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor. This medication is used to alleviate pain and swelling associated with specific types of arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It works by inhibiting a protein in the immune system called tumor necrosis factor (TNF), which is responsible for causing joint inflammation and damage. By reducing joint swelling, this medication helps prevent further joint damage and preserves joint function. Additionally, it is used to treat ulcerative colitis, a specific bowel condition. Before starting this medication, carefully read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Review these instructions each time you receive a refill. Consult your healthcare provider for guidance on how to prepare and administer this medication. It is typically injected under the skin once a month, as directed by your doctor. The injection can be administered in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition. For ulcerative colitis, your doctor may prescribe a different schedule or a higher dose at the beginning of treatment. Before injecting, remove the medication from the refrigerator at least 30 minutes in advance to allow it to reach room temperature. Do not warm the medication using other methods, such as microwaving or placing it in hot water. Avoid shaking the medication. Inspect the liquid for any cloudiness, large particles, or discoloration before use. If any of these are present, do not use the medication. The product may contain small, white, or translucent particles, which are normal. Before each injection, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate the injection site with each dose to minimize the risk of skin injury. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are sore, bruised, red, scaly, or hardened. To reduce bruising, do not rub the injection site after administering the medication. Use this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using this medication before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, and skin examinations, should be conducted. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. If necessary, it may be stored at room temperature. However, if stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator and discard it after 30 days. Dispose of any unused portion after use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. In a medical emergency, your condition may cause complications. Always inform healthcare providers about your condition and the medications you are using. This information was last revised in September 2024.
